source.title: AGD: an Auto-switchable Optimizer using Stepwise Gradient Difference for Preconditioning Matrix
source.authors: Yun Yue; Zhi-Ling Ye; Jiadi Jiang; Yongchao Liu; Ke Zhang

record.tranche_reason: Compares adaptive and non-adaptive optimizers on held-out benchmark performance, using a different optimizer and benchmark setup from the claim version.
record.gate_note: Optimizer comparison results bear on V4. AGD's switching analysis and its own optimizer results do not test the other claim versions. Training error is not reported, so the study does not test whether held-out differences occur despite equal or better training performance.
record.test_reason: The study compares held-out performance of adaptive optimizers and momentum SGD on image and language benchmarks. Its own baseline comparisons test V4 even though its main contribution is AGD. It is not an original source for V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that AGD outperforms other optimizers in most evaluated cases, provide convergence guarantees, and analyze its switching mechanism. This does not justify the record's challenges verdict for Adam versus SGD.
record.recipe_differences: Tests optimizer performance using AGD and benchmark comparisons, rather than the optimizer comparisons described in V4; weight decay is held the same across optimizers within each CV dataset.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and model change the relative result: Adam is below SGD on all three reported image-classification comparisons.

fits_no_version.finding: AGD's switching fractions, synthetic-function convergence trajectories and computational costs describe optimizer mechanisms and efficiency.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: AGD combines adaptive and SGD-like updates with competitive optimization performance and computational cost.

fits_no_version.finding: RecSys comparisons report held-out CTR AUC on Avazu and Criteo.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer performance also varies across recommendation workloads, outside V4's stated image and language benchmarks.

record.problems: Training error is not reported, so the comparison cannot establish whether held-out differences occur despite equal or better training performance. Results use the study's selected optimizer hyperparameters; the authors describe searches for optimal settings.
record.rows_left_out: No results were left out. The NLP and RecSys optimizer comparisons are not included because V4's benchmark conditions name image-classification and language benchmarks, while the table layout for individual NLP optimizer results is flattened and does not support a reliable assignment of values.

untested.parts: Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the role of local connectivity.

Whether held-out differences persist despite equal or better training performance; controlled limited-versus-broader tuning comparisons; recovery specifically by switching Adam to SGD. AdamW comparisons are reported, but differing learning rates prevent isolating decoupled weight decay's causal contribution.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptations under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout interventions; dropout is held fixed in language modeling.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps. Hessian-based optimizer design does not measure this relationship.

missing.what: Add adaptive-optimizer comparator rows from Table 4. AdamW accuracies are 92.12 ± .14, 92.72 ± .01 and 69.11 ± .17; AdaBelief: 92.19 ± .15, 92.90 ± .13 and 70.20 ± .03; AdaHessian: 92.27 ± .27, 92.91 ± .14 and 69.57 ± .12, in ResNet20/ResNet32/ResNet18 order. These reveal both deficits and exceptions relative to SGD.

The declared NLP omission should be repaired: Table 3's optimizer order is recoverable. For PTB one/two/three-layer LSTMs, SGD PPL is 85.36/67.26/63.68, Adam 84.50/67.01/64.45, AdamW 88.16/95.25/102.61, AdaBelief 84.40/66.69/61.34 and AdaHessian 88.62/73.37/69.51. Add rows with the reported uncertainties; language benchmarks are within V4.

record.verdict_notes: The central verdict is supports, not challenges. CV Adam/SGD settings were inherited; NLP includes epsilon tuning, so the study does not uniformly implement V4's limited-tuning protocol. NLP omissions were declared, but their stated unreadability is incorrect and they are listed for repair. IWSLT14's SGD BLEU 28.57 is explicitly borrowed from AdaHessian, so it cannot establish this study's own adaptive-versus-SGD result. AGD's superiority alone does not isolate recovery by switching.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Language benchmarks; broader tuning; optimizer switching or decoupled weight decay as recovery; training performance comparisons; Adam's word-level language-model advantage.
Large versus small batch training under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and its interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.
Effect of removing memorized training examples.

relationships.condition: Adam versus momentum SGD on CIFAR-10 ResNet20/32 and ImageNet ResNet18
relationships.reason: R1–R6 show SGD accuracy advantages of 1.68, 1.56 and 5.91 percentage points. Appendix A.1 uses inherited Adam/SGD configurations, rather than a controlled tuning-budget comparison.
relationships.display_finding: Momentum SGD exceeds Adam by 1.68, 1.56, and 5.91 accuracy points under inherited configurations, without a controlled tuning-budget comparison.

relationships.condition: AdamW and AdaBelief on CIFAR-10 ResNet20; AdaBelief on ImageNet ResNet18
relationships.reason: Table 4, not captured by adaptive-optimizer rows, shows near-equal ResNet20 accuracies for SGD/AdamW/AdaBelief (92.14/92.12/92.19), while ImageNet AdaBelief exceeds SGD (70.20 versus 69.94). The deficit depends on optimizer and workload.
